newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK POLICY MIX CAN'T PUSH INFLATION LOWER - IOBE.
newsitem.headline: GREEK POLICY MIX CAN'T PUSH INFLATION LOWER - IOBE.

text.p: Greece's economic policy mix has reached its limits as a mechanism for reducing inflation and can only produce small gains while increasing unemployment, said the private IOBE in its latest quarterly report.
The report called for an active supply side policy that should contain both structural changes and interventions and warned against mounting social discontent and reactions.
The drop in November inflation to 7.7 percent year-on-year from 8.3 percent in October does not signal a permanent downward trend since its core has not retreated, it said.

The Foundation of Industrial and Economic Research (IOBE) criticised the lack of progress in reducing primary expenditures and insufficient fiscal adjustment as reflected in the target-actual deficit figures.
Primary expenditures rose from 24.1 percent of GDP in 1994 to 25.3 percent of GDP in 1996 and are forecasted to climb to 25.8 percent in the 1997 budget, it said.

The borrowing requirement of the central government stood at 9.3 percent of GDP in 1996 from 10.5 percent in 1995 because of lower interest payments as a percentage of GDP and the small rise in the primary surplus, the offspring of a smaller investment budget deficit, it said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
